annotation.title_clean: Position Paper (China) on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems, CCW/GGE.1/2018/WP.7
annotation.title_en: Position Paper (China) on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems, CCW/GGE.1/2018/WP.7
annotation.authors_or_issuer: China (submission to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts, Geneva
annotation.summary_en: China's working paper to the 2018 CCW Group of Governmental Experts setting out its preliminary position on lethal autonomous weapons systems: a narrow definition with five characteristics, clarification of human-machine interaction, IHL applicability concerns, and caution against prejudging AI development.
key_provisions_or_claims: LAWS defined narrowly as fully autonomous lethal systems with five characteristics: lethality, autonomy, non-terminability, indiscriminate effect, evolution
Supports agreeing a definition starting from technical characteristics
Concepts like meaningful human control need further clarification
LAWS subject to IHL (distinction, proportionality, precaution) but application uncertain and accountability hard
National weapons reviews useful but cannot fundamentally solve LAWS concerns; avoid prejudging AI development
